newsitem.title: MOROCCO: MOROCCO'S BOURSE ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: MOROCCO'S BOURSE ENDS SLIGHTLY HIGHER.

text.p: Morocco's bourse continued higher on Thursday to close up 0.16 percent, boosted by the largest capitalisation firms, including Wafabank, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 657.83 points, up from 656.78 points on the previous session.
"Most stocks surged on Thursday as traders forecast good results for blue-chip firms this year, including the banking sector," a market analyst said.

Wafabank, a market blue-chip which performed well in recent weeks, rose five dirhams to close at 870 dirhams. The bank, which recently absorbed local Spanish Uniban bank, has a market capitalisation of 5.2 billion dirhams, the analyst said.
BMCE Bank, a liquid stock, gained six dirhams to close at 581 dirhams, he added.
Banque Marocaine pour le Developpement Economique, which is expected to be privatised soon, closed at 229 dirhams, up two dirhams over the previous trading session.
Oil refinery Samir, one of the market's largest capitalisation firm, was up three dirhams to close at 338 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, which has diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, ended the session at 761 dirhams compared with 760 on Wednesday.
Total trading volume continued to decline, to 54.7 million dirhams from 61.1 million dirhams on Wednesday.
Exchanges on the official market remained nearly unchanged at 21 million dirhams compared with the previous trading, brokers said.
